plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Microsemi / PowerDsine PoE midspans (MICROSEMI-PDSINE-MIB, enterprise PEN 7428). It reports uptime, supply voltage, maximum PoE power, internal / external power source status, unit temperature on 95xxG models, and interface traffic.
name: NetworkService

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Internal temperature of the Microsemi / PowerDsine PoE midspan in degrees Celsius, from temperature (MICROSEMI-PDSINE-MIB, 1.3.6.1.4.1.7428.1.2.2.1.1.11). Only Midspan 95xxG units have the sensor; temperatureformat (.12) decides Celsius or Fahrenheit, Fahrenheit readings are converted, and units reporting notsupported produce no series.

metrics.name: device_voltage_volts
metrics.description: Power supply voltage of the PoE midspan in volts, from mainVoltage (1.3.6.1.4.1.7428.1.2.2.1.1.2).

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: Internal and external power source status of the PoE midspan, from internalPowerSourceStatus (.9) and externalPowerSourceStatus (.10). ok maps to 1 (normal) and fail maps to 2 (abnormal); external sources reporting notsupported produce no series.

metrics.name: poe_max_power_watts
metrics.description: Maximum power the PoE midspan can deliver in watts after the power budget limit is applied, from mainPSEMaxPower (1.3.6.1.4.1.7428.1.2.2.1.1.5).

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of inbound bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of outbound bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
